title: Timothy and Titus (26 January)
hookLine: Paul's young companions, whom he trusted with churches

lines: BRING THE CLOAK AND THE BOOKS.
cards: Near the end of a letter, a prisoner adds a few errands. Hurry and come to me. Bring Mark with you.

And the cloak I left at Troas, bring that too, and the books, especially the parchments. The letter is Second Timothy, and the prisoner is Paul: an apostle in chains, wanting his coat, his books, and his friend.
The day after the feast of Paul's conversion, the Church keeps the feast of two people he trusted with whole churches. Timothy and Titus.

teach.h: TIMOTHY: FAITH FROM LOIS AND EUNICE.
teach.b: Start with Timothy. Acts says Paul met him in Lystra: a young disciple whose mother was a Jewish believer and whose father was Greek. Paul took him along on the road.
In the second letter, Paul remembers the faith that lived first in Timothy's grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice, and now in him.

Timothy's faith came across a kitchen table, from two women, before it ever met an apostle. Paul sent him to the churches when he couldn't go himself, and later left him to care for the church at Ephesus.

teach.h: DON'T LET THEM DESPISE YOUR YOUTH.
teach.b: He knew people might not take a young man seriously, so he wrote, in the Douay-Rheims: "Let no man despise thy youth: but be thou an example of the faithful". Now Titus.
Paul's letter to the Galatians says Titus was Greek.

teach.h: TITUS: SENT TO MEND, LEFT IN CRETE.
teach.b: Paul brought him to Jerusalem, sent him to Corinth to help mend a broken relationship, then left him on Crete to set things in order and appoint priests, elders, in every city.
Paul calls each of them his son in the faith.

teach.h: SONS BY YEARS ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Not by blood; by years on the road. The Catholic Church keeps them on one day, as bishops, close behind Paul.

teach.h: LET NO MAN DESPISE THY YOUTH.
teach.b: Some readers hear a quiet point in their feast: a church grows through the younger people an apostle trusted, kept writing to, and kept encouraging. Paul even tells Timothy to take a little wine for his stomach.
A mentor who notices your stomach means it.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Saints Timothy and Titus together, the day after the feast of the Conversion of Saint Paul, and the readings at Mass come from Paul's letters to them.

o: Paul's jailer, who later became a believer
Paul's young companion, trusted with Ephesus
a Greek apostle who wrote to the Galatians

games.q: Timothy and Titus — tap the pairs.

s: Paul calls Timothy and Titus his sons because they were his children
they were sons in the faith, by years on the road, not by blood.
Paul tells Timothy not to let anyone despise his youth
"let no man despise thy youth": and to be an example instead.
Paul's letter to the Galatians says Titus was Greek.

games.q: you're Paul. a church on Crete is in disorder and you can't stay. Titus is with you. what do you do?
o: leave Titus to set things in order and appoint elders.
write a letter and take Titus with you.
games.why: Paul says he left Titus in Crete to set things in order and appoint elders in every city, and then wrote to him.

practice: Bring to mind someone a step or two behind you, a new hire, a student, a niece starting out, someone who still gets talked over, and find one specific thing you've seen them do well: not a pep talk, one true detail.
If you pray, pray for them by name, the way Paul did for Timothy; if you don't, simply hold their name and the good thing you noticed.

wordCard.voice: Timothy, with Titus. Paul's young companions and fellow workers, whom he trusted with churches in Ephesus and Crete, and called his sons in the faith.

carryVoice: Your line: paul's sons. Faith passed hand to hand, older to younger. That's day nine hundred sixty-two.
